newsitem.title: USA: Foreign direct investment in US at record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreign direct investment in US at record in 1996.

text.p: Foreign investors spent a record $80.5 billion to buy or set up businesses in the United States during 1996, the Commerce Department said on Monday.
That was a 41 percent increase from the $57.2 billion spent a year earlier in 1995 by foreigners for the same purpose, either directly or through their existing U.S. affiliates.
Commerce said that foreign investment was more heavily aimed at service industries like finance, insurance and communications businesses during 1996 than was the case in past years.
"Outlays in manufacturing tended to be more concentrated in industries that are information-related or that use advanced technologies," the department said.
The number of investments exceeding $1 billion more than doubled to 19 from nine in 1995 and investments of $2 billion or more increased to eight in 1996 from five in 1995.
Commerce said that foreign investment was especially strong in U.S. business services including computer and data processing firms and health services providers.
The countries that were the most aggressive foreign buyers of U.S. businesses were Britain, Germany and Canada, which invested totals of $15.5 billion, $13 billion and $10.2 billion respectively.
Spending by Japanese investors was up for a third straight year, though at $9.3 billion in 1996 Japanese outlays were only about one-half of their 1990 peak of $19.9 billion.
Commerce said that Swiss investors cut their 1996 investments by $2.7 billion from 1995 to $4.8 billion.
